info.title: Yuvomi API
info.description: OpenAPI documentation for the Yuvomi family organizer backend.

get.description: Public bootstrap metadata for login/setup, including `product` and `client_api`, which let a client recognise an instance and tell whether it is new enough before anyone signs in. When a valid session or API token is supplied, the response also includes the exact app version and `max_upload_bytes`. A client probing an instance sends no credential: an invalid one answers 401.

200.description: Authenticated user and CSRF token, or the request for a second factor

post.description:
With two-factor authentication turned on, a right password opens no session yet: the response is `{ twoFactorRequired, recoveryAvailable }`, and POST /auth/2fa/verify completes the sign-in.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `account_cannot_sign_in` (403, the account is deactivated or may not sign in), `password_login_disabled` (403, password login is turned off for this instance).

post.summary: Complete sign-in with a second factor

400.description: The code is longer than 64 characters

401.description: Invalid code, or no pending sign-in

403.description: The account may no longer sign in, for example because it was deactivated in the meantime (`reason: "account_cannot_sign_in"`). No recovery code is spent.

post.description:
Second step after POST /auth/login answered with `twoFactorRequired`. Accepts either the six-digit TOTP code or one of the recovery codes; the response says which one was used. The pending sign-in expires after five minutes.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `two_factor_no_pending_sign_in` (401, no sign-in is waiting for a code, or it has expired), `account_cannot_sign_in` (403, the account is deactivated or may not sign in).

200.description: The ways in this server offers

get.description: Public login-page bootstrap endpoint. Returns which ways in this server offers: whether OIDC is configured and enabled, and whether password login is allowed (AUTH_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN, ignored unless OIDC is fully configured). The login page waits for this single answer before painting, so it never shows a form that then disappears. guest_password_login_enabled is true only where password login is off AND the household actually has split-expense guests, who are exempt from the switch (#847) because they are external people with no account in the household identity provider. It is one bit and says nothing about who or how many; where password login is open the question is moot and the field is false.

201.description: Device added. The plaintext credential is returned only once.

post.description:
Exchanges a sign-in for a device credential, the bearer a native client uses from then on. A device acts as the person, with less reach than a browser session: an administrator is an ordinary member on it, and of `/api/v1/auth` it reaches only `GET /me`, `GET /users`, `GET /oidc/config`, `POST /logout`, `GET /devices` and `DELETE /devices/{id}`; anything else answers 403 with `reason: device_credential`. It ends after 90 days without use, and with everything that ends a session. The same `device_id` replaces the earlier credential.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `device_credential` (403, a device cannot add another device), `session_required` (403, an API token cannot add a device), `not_a_household_member` (403, the account is no household member).

post.description:
Exchanges a pairing code for a device credential. Public, the code is the proof. Send no `Authorization` header: a valid device credential is refused here. Unknown, expired and used codes answer alike, and so does the code of an account that can no longer have a device. Attempts are limited.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `invalid_pairing_code` (400, the code is unknown, expired, used, or its account can no longer have a device), `device_credential` (403, the request carried a valid device credential).

200.description: The data of the overview. Depending on module access it can carry further fields that are not described here.

get.description: Aggregated data for every overview tile. Optional query parameters filter tasks, upcoming events and pinned notes before row limits and counts are computed. Task filters apply to every task slice (`urgentTasks`, `openTaskCount`, `overdueTaskCount`, `memberTodayTasks`, `tasksDoneToday`, `wallTasks`); note filters apply to `pinnedNotes`, `pinnedNotesCount` and `notesTotal` alike. Event filters apply to both `upcomingEvents` and `weekEvents` (the events touching the household days from yesterday to a week ahead, in a compact shape for the week strip of the calendar tile). The browser derives these filters from per-widget `options` stored in `dashboard_widgets`. `upcomingEvents` counts only appointments that have not ended toward its five-item cap; already ended ones of today (end before now in the household time zone, never all-day ones) come along outside the cap. `familyEvents` feeds the Family card: per household member the appointments of today (ended ones included) and the next coming ones, merged once; the `events_scope` filter does not apply to it, `events_birthdays` does. `wallTasks` feeds wall mode: per household member the tasks of today by title (`open`: not done and due today or earlier; `done`: done and due today, or overdue and ticked off today in the household time zone), at most six titles each next to the uncapped `open_count` and `done_count`. Unlike every other task slice it carries only tasks with visibility `all`, whoever the caller is: a wall tablet is not a person. `wastePickups` lists the collections of today and tomorrow (Waste module), `myShiftsToday` the own shifts of the caller of today (Schedule module); both are empty when the module is denied. `splitBalance` (`{ net, positions }`) lists what the caller has open in shared expenses: net per currency and each open position from the settle-up view of the caller's active groups (the same balances as `GET /split-expenses/groups/{id}/balances`), household currency first; it is empty without `budget` read access. A module the household has switched off (`disabled_modules` in `/preferences`) is left out the same way as a denied one: its fields stay in the response with their empty values. `birthdays` is a switch of its own here, so the birthday fields follow it rather than the `calendar` switch, and `upcomingEvents`, `weekEvents` and `familyEvents` carry no birthday events while it is off.

parameters.name: notes_category
parameters.description: Limit pinned notes to those carrying every selected category (AND). Repeatable positive category IDs, deduplicated and capped at 50. Omitted or empty means all visible pinned notes. Only household categories and the caller's own personal categories may match; another user's personal category cannot reveal notes.

parameters.name: tasks_category
parameters.description: Limit tasks to these categories. Repeatable; several values combine with OR. Omitted or empty means every category.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description: `household` asks for the version for a shared surface (wall mode): an allowlist. The response then carries only the keys a wall draws: `users`, `upcomingEvents`, `birthdays`, `urgentTasks`, `tasksDoneToday`, `wallTasks`, `todayMeals`, `shoppingOpenCount`, `wastePickups`, of `pantryExpiring` the fields `todayItems` and `todayCount`, and of `housekeeping` the fields `present`, `presentSince` and `workerName`. Tasks and appointments in them are those the whole household may see - visibility `all`, appointments from ICS subscriptions only from shared ones - whoever the caller is, creator and assignees included; `events_scope=mine` is ignored. Every other key keeps its place in the same empty form as for a caller without the module - notes, `budget`, `splitBalance`, `quicklinks`, `countdowns`, the counters and week/family slices of tasks and calendar, `housekeeping.unpaidAmount`, and what belongs to the caller alone (`health`, `fasting`, `nutrition`, `myShiftsToday`, `rewards`); `shoppingTile` is absent. A key added to this response later is empty for this audience until it is put on the list. The parameter only narrows the response, so it needs no scope of its own. Anything else means the personal version.

parameters.name: events_scope
parameters.description: `mine` limits appointments to those assigned to the calling user - among the assignees, so an unassigned event is not "mine" (same reading as the calendar module). A paired display has no assignments of its own, so for it `mine` reads as all appointments. Anything else means all appointments.

parameters.name: events_birthdays
parameters.description: `hide` drops appointments that belong to a birthday entry from `upcomingEvents` and `weekEvents`, so a household that already shows the Birthdays tile does not read them twice. Applied before the cap (`events_limit`), so the freed rows are filled with the next real appointments. Anything else keeps them - birthdays are in by default.

parameters.name: shopping_list
parameters.description: Which lists the shopping tile shows. Repeatable positive list IDs, deduplicated and capped at 50. The selection applies to the tile only: with it the response carries an extra field `shoppingTile` = `{ lists, openCount, listCount }` - the selected lists (at most three, also those without open items, lists with open items first, each with up to six open items), the open items within the selection, and how many selected lists exist. `shoppingLists`, `shoppingOpenCount` and `shoppingOpenLists` are never affected and keep counting across all lists. IDs of lists that do not exist are dropped; when none of the IDs exists, or the value is not an ID, the request answers like one without the parameter and `shoppingTile` is absent. A caller without access to shopping gets the empty shopping payload and no `shoppingTile`.

parameters.name: events_calendar
parameters.description: Which calendars the appointments come from, under the keys of the calendar module: `local:<id>` for an own calendar, `cal:<id>` for a synced one (CalDAV, Google), `sub:<id>` for an ICS subscription - the `key` values of `sources` from `GET /calendar/calendars`, the catalogue the selection is checked against. Repeatable, deduplicated and capped at 50; a value of any other shape is dropped. Applies to `upcomingEvents` and `weekEvents` before the cap (`events_limit`), not to `familyEvents`. Appointments that belong to no calendar (birthdays, housekeeping visits) always pass; birthdays have `events_birthdays`. Keys the caller cannot choose (a deleted calendar, a removed subscription, a disconnected account, another member's private subscription) are dropped; when none is left the request answers like one without the parameter, never with an empty list.

parameters.name: events_limit
parameters.description: How many upcoming appointments `upcomingEvents` lists: `5`, `8` or `12`. The value is matched against exactly these three; anything else - omitted, empty, repeated, `7`, `500` - means `5`. Appointments of today that have already ended come on top and do not count against it. `weekEvents` and `familyEvents` are not affected.

200.description: Top-level tasks, sorted by status, priority and due date

get.description: Several tags narrow the result: a task must carry all of them. Tag matching ignores case, including non-ASCII letters. Archived tasks are omitted unless asked for. `document_count` counts the linked documents the caller may see; `GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}` also carries them as `documents`. Without access to the Documents module (for API tokens a `documents:read` scope) both are `null` - not told, which is not the same as `0` or an empty list. A rotating task (`rotation_mode: "round_robin"`, fixed order only, #1763) additionally carries `rotation_pool` (member ids in delivery order, `null` when the task does not rotate), `rotation_last_user` (informational - which member the pointer names), `rotation_last_position` (the pointer: the pool position of the last recipient; the order reads the position, never the head, so a member leaving the pool does not restart the series) and `rotation_next_user` - the member the next occurrence would go to, resolved by the same rule that hands out the next instance (pointer plus one in pool order, over the gaps of departed members and the slots of deactivated ones), `null` when rotation is off or fewer than two members are active.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Repeatable; several values are OR-ed. "archived" is not a status but the separate archive axis and behaves like the `archived` parameter.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Archived tasks are hidden by default. `1` includes them, `only` returns just the archive. A task keeps its own status while archived.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeat once per tag (?tag=a&tag=b). Each occurrence is one literal tag, never a comma-separated list, so a tag containing a comma survives.

parameters.name: include_future

post.description:
Body accepts `locked: true` to close the task definition to everyone but its creator and administrators (#830). A subtask under a locked parent inherits the lock, and adding one requires the same rights. `status` may be set on creation (#807); it runs through the same transition handling as PUT and PATCH, so creating a task as `done` books its points and writes its completion entry. `null`, an empty string and `archived` all fall back to `open` - filing a task away is a separate axis and not something a creation can do. Rotation: `rotation_mode: "round_robin"` (the only mode - a fixed order, not a set, #1763) with `rotation_pool` (array of member ids, the list order is the delivery order) hands every follow-up instance to the next member. A mode requires a recurring task and a pool of at least 2 known household members, anything else answers 400.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `tasks_parent_not_found` (404, `parent_task_id` names a task that does not exist or is not visible to you).

put.description:
On a locked task (`locked: 1`) only the creator and administrators may change the definition - title, description, category, priority, dates, recurrence, points, visibility, tags, sync target, the lock itself, and assigning other members. Everyone else may still send the full body as long as the outcome differs only in `status` or in their own entry in `assigned_to`; anything else answers 403. The comparison is against the stored values, not against which fields were sent. Rotation fields follow the rule of the rest of the body: absent means untouched; `rotation_mode: null` clears mode, pool and pointer together. Sending only `rotation_pool` re-deals the pool positions but keeps the pointer, so an edited order continues the rotation from where it stands instead of resetting it; changing the mode starts the round fresh. Returns `{ data: Task }`; the task additionally carries `next_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) under the same rule as PATCH /tasks/{id}/status: the due date of the next occurrence still pending and visible to the caller when this call moved a recurring task into `done`, and `null` in every other case - no status change, a change that is not a transition into `done`, a task without recurrence, a series that has ended, or a next occurrence the caller cannot see.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `tasks_task_not_found` (404, the task does not exist or is not visible to you - deleted, or made private), `task_foreign_series` (409, the task repeats in another app with a rule Yuvomi cannot follow - it is in `external_rrule` - and is ticked off there, #2506).

patch.description:
Body: { status, done_by_user_id? }. Sending `archived` files the task away without touching its status - use PATCH /archive instead. Deliberately open on a locked task: ticking one off is the interaction the lock exists to preserve. `done_by_user_id` names who actually did the task (#1205), which is not necessarily the caller - on a shared tablet it rarely is. It has to be a household member (400 otherwise), it only applies to the transition into `done` and is ignored on any other status change, and it decides where the points go: a named member who takes part in rewards receives them instead of the assignees, a named member who does not take part means no points at all rather than crediting someone who did not do it. Omit it and nothing changes: the history shows the caller and the assignees rule applies. The naming is as idempotent as the completion itself - correcting it means reopening the task and ticking it off again. A paired wall display reaches this route too, and only this one of the writing routes (#1209): for it the field is required rather than optional, only the transition into `done` is allowed, and the task has to be visible to the whole household, which answers 404 rather than 403 so an invisible task is not confirmed to exist. Returns `{ data: { id, status, archived_at, next_due_date } }`. `next_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) is the due date of the next occurrence still pending - not done and not archived, so one that is `in_progress` counts - when this call completed a recurring task, and `null` in every other case: a task without recurrence, a series that has ended, a status change that is not a transition into `done`, and the `archived` shortcut, which omits the field.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `tasks_task_not_found` (404, the task does not exist or is not visible to you - deleted, or made private), `display_action` (403, a paired display can only tick a task off), `task_foreign_series` (409, the task repeats in another app with a rule Yuvomi cannot follow - it is in `external_rrule` - and is ticked off there, #2506).

get.summary: Change counter of every shopping list
get.description: One `{ list_id, version }` per list. The counter says *that* a list changed, never *what*: it moves whenever the list was renamed or its items were inserted, updated, moved or deleted by anyone - a household member, a meal-plan import, the CalDAV sync - and the row disappears with the list. Database triggers keep it, so no writer has to announce itself. A client polls this while a list is open and reloads a list through the same items request it used to open it; the write routes on items return `list_change: { list_id, before, after }` so the writer can tell its own change apart.

Contract change (#1103): response items are now objects { name, category, quantity } instead of plain name strings (string[] before), and the list is ordered by most recently used first instead of alphabetically. Category and quantity come from the most recent item row with that name - the latest statement about how the household files the article today.

patch.description: Body: { is_checked?, name?, quantity?, category?, notes?, url?, price_cents?, store_id?, list_id? } - a field that is not sent stays as it is. `list_id` moves the item to another list: it keeps its name, quantity, category, note, link, price and shop, and goes to the end of its category on the list it lands on. `list_id` and `store_id` are positive integers, as a number or a string of digits; anything else and an unknown `list_id` are refused with 400 and nothing changes, as is a move to a list with `accepts_new_items: 0`. If the item is mirrored from a CalDAV list and the target list is mirrored too, its object on the server moves along after the response, unchanged and under the same UID; if the target list is not mirrored, the object is removed on the server and its mirrored tags are dropped. `list_change` in the response names the list the item came from. A case a household member can run into carries a machine-readable `reason` next to `error`: `shopping_item_not_found` (404, the item is gone), `shopping_list_not_found` (400, unknown `list_id`), `shopping_store_not_found` (400, unknown `store_id`), `shopping_category_not_found` (400, unknown `category`). Every shopping route that works on a list answers a missing list with 404 and `reason: "shopping_list_not_found"`. Validation errors carry no `reason`.

get.description: Events generated from the birthdays module carry `birthday_name` and `birthday_date` (null for a birthday whose year is unknown, `year_unknown` on the birthday). Their `title` is stored in the household data language (see `language` in `/preferences`), so API consumers, the ICS feed and calendar sync all read the same wording; clients that display in a different language can re-render the title from `birthday_name`. While the household has the birthdays module switched off (`disabled_modules` in `/preferences`), these events are left out of this list, of `/calendar/upcoming`, of `/calendar/search` and of the ICS feed; a single one stays reachable by id, and the birthdays routes keep answering. A series comes as one row per occurrence in the range, all with the `id` of the series; `series_id` and `recurrence_id` tell them apart.

post.description:
Supports optional document-storage attachments via `attachment_name`, `attachment_mime`, `attachment_size`, and `attachment_data` (base64 data URL). New attachments are linked through `attachment_document_id`; legacy events may still return `attachment_data`. Set `target_caldav_account_id` and `target_caldav_calendar_url` to push the event to a CalDAV calendar (omit or null for a local-only event). A new attachment creates a document in the Documents module and therefore needs write access there (member right, for API tokens a `documents:write` scope); without it any non-empty `attachment_data` is refused with 403 before the event is looked up. Replacing or removing an attachment needs read access to the Documents module and sight of the stored document; otherwise the same 403, and the attachment stays. The 403 bodies carry `reason` `ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_REFUSED` or `ATTACHMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED`. Saving an event carries its visibility and assignees over to the attachment's document only when the save changes who sees the event (its visibility, or the assignees of an event for assignees); a save of the title, time or other fields leaves the document's visibility and shares alone. It opens the document further only for a caller with write access to documents who can see it and may manage it (its creator - for an attachment the event creator - or an admin); otherwise the document keeps the visibility and shares its owner set, so the save neither opens nor narrows it and removes no share. A new attachment uploaded in the same save to an event the caller did not create is only narrowed to the event, never opened further. The default-assignee sync of connected calendars never changes document rights, with one exception: when the event is visible to its assignees and the document is already shared with selected members, the new assignee is added to those shares. Otherwise nothing changes - no document becomes visible to the family, none is opened, narrowed or made private, and no share is removed. A copy made on split or detach belongs to the owner of its source document. A split or a detach copies the attachment for the new series or event only for such a caller; otherwise the new one has no attachment and the original stays on the original series. `start_datetime` and `end_datetime` take the forms of `CalendarDateOrDateTimeInput`: a value without offset is household wall-clock time, a value with `Z` or a numeric offset is read as an instant and converted into the household time zone (`2026-09-21T16:00:00Z` in a Europe/Berlin household is stored as `2026-09-21T18:00`). For an all-day event only the date of such a value counts. Up to v2.68.0 the offset was dropped and its digits kept as wall-clock time. A `recurrence_rule` whose `UNTIL` day lies before the start day is rejected with 400 (`recurrence_rule: the series ends before the start date.`, `reason: calendar_series_ends_before_start`); an `UNTIL` on the start day is a series with one occurrence and is accepted. PUT checks this only when the request changes the rule or the start day, so an imported series that already carries such a rule stays editable; the start day is compared as the household calendar day, so sending the wall-clock form of a stored instant is not a change. For an event with a time zone of its own, whose stored UTC day differs from its local day, only a changed rule is checked, and only an `UNTIL` before both days is rejected. ICS import and calendar sync do not reject it.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `calendar_selected_calendar_not_found` (400, the `local_calendar_id` names a local calendar that no longer exists), `calendar_series_no_occurrence` (400, the `recurrence_rule` has no occurrence on or after the start date), `calendar_series_ends_before_start` (400, its `UNTIL` lies before the start day).

get.description:
The caller's own reminders that are not due yet, for a client that schedules them on the device. Both edges of the window count, and it spans at most 14 days. Only what lies after the current moment comes back, also when `from` is in the past: a reminder is in `GET /reminders/pending` from the moment it is due and in this list until then, never in both. Sorted by the moment the reminder fires, at most 200 rows, counted after everything the caller may not see is left out. The list is a snapshot: the server keeps rebuilding derived types, and it does not know what a client scheduled.

The rules of `GET /reminders/pending` apply: own, non-dismissed rows only, nothing whose entity is hidden from the caller, no task or event that is gone, no reminder of a series whose first occurrence was deleted, nothing from a module the household switched off, and only origins the caller may read. On top of them, a task that is done or archived is left out, and comes back when it is reopened: what a client schedules fires without asking again. A client still has to cancel its own notification when a task is checked off, because this list only changes at the next fetch. An API token needs `calendar:read` to reach this route and a read scope of the module behind each origin for its rows, for example `tasks:read` for `task`; a row the caller may not read is left out, not refused.

Use `fires_at`, not `remind_at`, to schedule: `remind_at` is UTC without a suffix, and rows written up to v2.68.0 may carry an offset.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the window, included. At most 14 days after `from`. Without `Z` or an offset the value is UTC, as in `remind_at`; a date alone is midnight UTC; fractions of a second are dropped. Percent-encode a `+` in an offset (`%2B`): unencoded it reads as a space and answers 400.

product.description: Identifies a Yuvomi instance. `app_name` cannot do that: a household can rename it.

client_api.description: The contract a native client relies on. It rises only when a client cannot work without the change, not with every release, so a client can tell a server that is too old before anyone signs in. 0 means no contract yet. 1 covers signed-in devices and pairing, `GET /reminders/upcoming` with `fires_at`, and the operations a native client is built from.

password_reset_enabled.description: True when self-service password reset can actually deliver a mail (SMTP configured AND BASE_URL set) and there are passwords to reset at all (AUTH_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN not switched off). The login page gates the "forgot password" link on this flag so it is never a dead end.

max_upload_bytes.description: The largest upload this server accepts. Only with a valid credential, like `version`: before sign-in there is nothing to upload.

bearerAuth.description: API token sent in the Authorization header as `Bearer <token>`.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: API token sent in the `X-API-Key` header. `API-Key` is also accepted for MCP compatibility.

cookieAuth.name: yuvomi.sid
cookieAuth.description: Browser session cookie. State-changing requests also require `X-CSRF-Token`.
